articles.body: One version of my evaluator passed a Kubernetes configuration whose selector contradicted its own pod labels. It also rejected a configuration just because an extra label had been added. Both results were scoring errors. If you are new to evals, start with What exactly are AI evals? . It explains the tasks, graders, and metrics used in this case study. These came up while working on IaC Eval Bench , a small project for evaluating model-generated Kubernetes configurations. A scoring review found five mistakes in the evaluator, even though its original reference and negative-control examples were producing the expected totals. That last part is worth explaining. A passing test suite tells us that the cases we wrote behave as expected.

articles.excerpt: I pay for more than one coding agent. They're good at different things, and sometimes I just want a second opinion on what the first one wrote. The annoying part was never switching tools. It was re-e…
articles.body: I pay for more than one coding agent. They're good at different things, and sometimes I just want a second opinion on what the first one wrote. The annoying part was never switching tools. It was re-explaining the task every time. So in Coincide , my open-source (MIT) Mac app for coding agents, a thread isn't tied to one agent. You type /codex (or pick a Codex model), and Codex continues the conversation Claude Code started, in the same folder. Switch back, and Claude Code picks up its own session again. Here's how that works. Everything below is in the repo , mostly in Handoff.swift . Six agents, six protocols Coincide doesn't call model APIs.

articles.title: I attempted 2,000 pull-ups. The next morning, I open-sourced my timer.
articles.excerpt: Paused at 1,124, during a "service stop" (my name for the breaks between blocks). On October 24, I attempted 2,000 pull-ups in eight hours. I stopped at 1,124, about five hours and twenty minutes in.…
articles.body: Paused at 1,124, during a "service stop" (my name for the breaks between blocks). On October 24, I attempted 2,000 pull-ups in eight hours . I stopped at 1,124 , about five hours and twenty minutes in. That was 124 more than my previous personal record. It was also 876 short of the goal. A failed attempt. Both belong in the record. I ran the whole session on an EMOM timer I had built inside my portfolio. EMOM means every minute on the minute : at the top of each minute, do the planned reps, then rest for whatever is left of it. The next morning, I started extracting that timer into a free, open-source app. It now runs at emom-pullups.vercel.app . No account. Your training data stays in your browser.

articles.title: How to Find the Questions Your Customers Ask Before They Buy
articles.excerpt: Originally published on the ATLAS AEO blog, where you can also read it in 10 other languages. Quick answer: To find the questions your customers ask before they buy, start with the questions they alre…
articles.body: Originally published on the ATLAS AEO blog , where you can also read it in 10 other languages. Quick answer: To find the questions your customers ask before they buy, start with the questions they already ask you: sales calls, emails, contact forms, reviews and your site's search box. Then add what people type into search: Google Search Console queries, autocomplete and "People also ask". Group the questions by buying stage, rank them by how often they come up and how close they are to a sale, and answer the top ones on your own pages. Key takeaways Your best content ideas are questions real customers already ask your team. Write them down word for word. Search Console shows the exact queries that already bring you impressions, including questions you have never answered on purpose.

In this blog, we will delve into the concept of Fiber trees and explore how the reconciliation process works. articles.body: The original Fable checked all of the boxes of a good fairy tale: a classic good-versus-evil tale set in a high-fantasy version of Fake Britain. You played as a hero (literally, the “Hero of Oakvale”) fighting against a guy who considered burning down villages his idea of a good time. Fable ’s big innovation lay in its morality system: Depending on your actions, the hero’s appearance would change (ex: you’d grow devil horns if you were evil), as would the way the citizens of Albion would react to him. Just like the main characters of stories like Jack and the Beanstalk , Little Red Riding Hood , and other quintessential fairy tales, you were consigned to live with the consequences of your actions — good or bad.

It’s a shame, considering how beloved the Metroid Prime series has been since the first title’s 2002 debut for the Nintendo GameCube. articles.excerpt: Satellites are watching fireballs blaze through Earth's atmosphere, strengthening planetary defense knowhow and helping scientists learn more about space debris impacts.
articles.body: It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 1, 1962: The Soviet Union Launches Mars 1 spacecraft to Red Planet during the Space Race
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. While it did end up flying by Mars , the mission was not exactly a success. After it separated from the rocket, it deployed its solar panels and started cruising toward Mars. When mission controllers were checking out the telemetry it transmitted back to Earth, they found out that Mars 1 had sprung a leak in one of the gas valves that controls the spacecraft's orientation. And without a working orientation system, Mars 1 would have a hard time pointing its antennas in the right direction. It lost contact with Earth when it was about halfway to Mars . A model of Mars 1, a Mars flyby spacecraft launched to the Red Planet by the Soviet Union on Nov. 1, 1962.

articles.body: This is a great month for planet watching, either in the evenings or mornings. During convenient evening hours, the planet of choice is Saturn , visible well up in the southern sky during mid-to-late evening hours. Telescopically, the southern side of its famous ring system is currently tilted about 6½ degrees to our line of sight. Around the middle of the night, Mars and Jupiter come into view above the east-northeast horizon and just before the break of dawn are in excellent position, soaring high in the southern sky in the vicinity of the Sickle of Leo the Lion. Watch how Mars approaches Jupiter early in the month, passes it on Nov. 16, then spends the rest of the month sailing away to the east.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
